...Thru the Bible - Questions & Answers  Dr. J. Vernon McGee...

2) Who are the 24 elders in Revelation 5:13-14?

3) What does the phrase "may the Lord do so and much more" mean in 1 Samuel 20:13?

4) Do the events in 2 Samuel 2:15-16 describe some type of sacrificial rite that had to be performed before the battle could begin?

6) Why did Jesus need to study the Scriptures since as God He would know all things?

7) Is it possible to be a born-again believer and never be filled with the Holy Spirit?

https://ttb.org/

...Thru the Bible - Minute with McGee Dr. J. Vernon McGee...

Good things ahead

You know, friends, that the child of God has some great things in store for the future. I think that the redeemed are going to occupy actually exalted positions. I wonder if you’re working for a place. Somebody says, “Well, I didn’t think you work for salvation.” You don’t work for salvation. But let me put it like this. You don’t work for heaven, but you work for your place in heaven. You’re going to heaven by the grace of God, but you’re going to be judged according to your works to see what position that you have. Are you interested in your good works then? You ought to be—that which is done by the Spirit of God.

References: Luke 22:1-34

https://www.oneplace.com/ministries/thru-the-bible-minute-with-mcgee/listen/good-things-ahead-1296553.html

https://ttb.org/

...Daily Promises...

To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins. (Acts 10:43)

Rejoice in your justified state, you who believe! Even the prophets of old marvel at the proclamation of the forgiveness that would be bought you! Yours is the gift eternal! Yours is the very life of the Slain Lamb! Your future is assured and none may thwart your eternal and heavenly life. Again I say rejoice, believer! Rejoice and go forth in His Spirit in all righteousness!

https://www.blueletterbible.org/devotionals/promises/view.cfm

And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. — Mark 4:39

The wind may blow and the rain may fall, but the Master can still bring peace into the middle of your storm.
